newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Explorers Index continues to weaken.
newsitem.headline: Australian Explorers Index continues to weaken.

text.p: Perth stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd said its Australian Explorers Index fell sharply for the third consecutive week, with a fall of 41.8 points or 1.30 percent. The All Ordinaries Index rose 2.16 percent. Changes, in percent:
Jun 20 Jun 13 pct 1 Month pct 1 Year pct
NOTE: The explorers index (base 500, March 1992) tracks the performance of 88 small capitalisation exploration companies.
Since May 30, the explorers index has fallen by a total of 177.90 points, or 5.3 percent. In the same time, the All Ordinaries Index has risen 102.1 points, or 3.9 percent.
Eyres Reed analyst Glen Colgan said in a commentary that tax selling and stale traders weighed heavily on junior resources despite a stronger blue chip market. Falls outnumber gains by two to one.

Joint venture partners in the Mt Kare project in Papua New Guinea, Ramsgate Resources NL and Carpenter Pacific Resources NL were sold down despite further good results from the prospect and assurance that any diminution of
their interests by the PNG government would be shared by their Canadian partner, Madison Enterprises Corp.
Ramsgate fell three cents to eight cents and Carpenter dropped 16.5 cents to 29 cents.
Oil and gas juniors Anzoil NL and Frontier Petroleum NL were both weaker, with Anzoil off 1.1 cents to 4.9 cents and Frontier down one cent to 4.3 cents.
Diamond explorer Striker Resources NL fell two cents to 11.5 percent and Leo Shield Exploration NL dropped six cents to 44 cents following the announcement of a proposed placement.

Other falls included Jubliee Gold Mines NL down five cents to 16.5 cents, Bendigo Mining NL off six cents to 27 cents, Nexus Minerals NL down 3.5 cents to 12 cents and Cluff Resources Pacific NL dropped 0.9 cents to 3.4 cents.

The strongest gains included Consolidated Gold NL up 11.5 cents to 34.5 cents, Victoria Petroleum NL up 3.5 percent to 18 cents, Roebuck Resources NL up 10 cents to 78 cents, and Western Reefs Ltd up seven cents to 47 cents.
Murchison United NL jumped 19 cents to 78 cents after announcing positive results from their Indonesian coal venture.
